title: Rock Star Abuja: Zuma at First Light
summary: Zuma Rock sits just outside the capital in Niger State, a bald granite lump rising out of flat farmland. We get there before the heat, walk the footpaths around its base with a Gbagyi guide who knows which stories are folklore and which are family history, and eat a late breakfast of yam and egg from a roadside stall.

seo.metaTitle: Rock Star Abuja: Zuma at First Light | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The boulder everyone films from a car window. 6 hours small-group tour in Abuja, Nigeria.

title: Two Domes, One Skyline: Abuja's Big Buildings
summary: Abuja was planned from scratch in the 1980s, and the two largest places of worship sit almost within sight of each other. You tour the National Mosque and the National Christian Centre with a guide who explains the design choices, then climb for a view of Aso Rock and the Three Arms Zone.

seo.metaTitle: Two Domes, One Skyline: Abuja's Big Buildings | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Mosque, church and the hill behind them. 4 hours small-group tour in Abuja, Nigeria.

title: Clay Hands at Ushafa
summary: Ushafa village is home to a pottery centre that carries on the work of Ladi Kwali, the Gwari potter who ended up on the old twenty naira note. You spend a morning with working potters, try coiling a pot yourself, and leave with something slightly lopsided to carry home.

seo.metaTitle: Clay Hands at Ushafa | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Throw a pot where Ladi Kwali**'**s legacy lives. 5 hours small-group tour in Abuja, Nigeria.

title: Gurara Falls Day Out
summary: Gurara is less a plunge than a broad curtain spread across a rock shelf, and from the right viewpoint it looks like a small Niagara. The drive from Abuja takes about two hours, and we stop in a village on the way for kola and fried plantain before the walk down.

seo.metaTitle: Gurara Falls Day Out | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Wide water, flat rocks, packed lunch. 9 hours small-group tour in Niger State, Nigeria.

title: Lake Jabi at Dusk
summary: The lake is where Abuja residents go once work is done. We arrive late afternoon, walk the shoreline path past fishing canoes and picnic parties, and finish with grilled fish on the lakeside while the sky turns orange over the Jabi towers.

seo.metaTitle: Lake Jabi at Dusk | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Joggers, kites and a very good sunset. 3 hours small-group tour in Abuja, Nigeria.

title: Wuse Market Without the Stress
summary: Wuse Market is loud, crowded and exactly the sort of place where a guide earns their fee. You learn to read the fabric stalls, pick out proper ankara from knock-offs, haggle without insulting anyone, and finish with pepper soup at a small canteen tucked behind the main aisles.

seo.metaTitle: Wuse Market Without the Stress | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A guided pass through Abuja**'**s busiest stalls. 4 hours small-group tour in Abuja, Nigeria.

title: Lekki Canopy Walk and the Swamp Below
summary: The Lekki Conservation Centre has one of the longest tree-canopy walkways in Africa, strung through swamp forest a short drive from the shopping malls. We walk it slowly, look for monkeys and monitor lizards, then circle the nature trails while the guide names the birds.

seo.metaTitle: Lekki Canopy Walk and the Swamp Below | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Hang above the swamp forest. 4 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Makoko by Canoe
summary: Makoko is a stilt community on the lagoon with its own schools, fishing trade and boat builders. You paddle through with a resident guide who sets the ground rules, watch fish being smoked on the water's edge, and hear how the community deals with eviction threats and rising tides.
highlights: Third Mainland Bridge from the water

seo.metaTitle: Makoko by Canoe | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The floating neighbourhood, seen with permission. 3 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Freedom Park: Prison Walls, Poetry Nights
summary: Freedom Park on Lagos Island occupies the old Broad Street Prison, and the cell blocks are still there beneath the lawns and stages. We walk the former yard with a guide who tells the prison's history, then settle in for whatever performance or reading is on that evening.

seo.metaTitle: Freedom Park: Prison Walls, Poetry Nights | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: From colonial jail to open-air stage. 3 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Tarkwa Bay: Learn to Stand on a Board
summary: Tarkwa Bay is sheltered by the harbour breakwater, so the waves are gentle enough for first-timers. A short boat ride from the mainland gets you there; a local instructor handles the lesson, and lunch is grilled fish on the sand.

seo.metaTitle: Tarkwa Bay: Learn to Stand on a Board | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Beginner surf, no show-offs. 6 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Lagos Brazilian Quarter: Houses That Came Back Across the Atlantic
summary: Freed Africans returning from Brazil in the 1800s brought a building style with them: plastered facades, arched windows, ornate balconies. We walk the Popo Aguda area, step inside the Shitta-Bey Mosque, and look for the surviving houses between newer buildings.

seo.metaTitle: Lagos Brazilian Quarter: Houses That Came Back Across the Atlantic | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Returnee architecture on Lagos Island. 4 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Eko Atlantic and the Great Wall of Lagos
summary: Eko Atlantic is being raised on land reclaimed from the Atlantic, protected by an enormous sea wall. A guide walks you through the planning story and the debate around it, and you stop at the wall itself where the ocean pushes right up to the rock.

seo.metaTitle: Eko Atlantic and the Great Wall of Lagos | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A city being built on ocean floor. 3 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Epe Smoked Fish and Lagoon Lunch
summary: Epe, on the edge of Lagos State, is known for its smoked and dried fish. You watch the women who run the smoking racks, take a short boat ride on the lagoon, and eat what came out of the water that morning with pounded yam.

seo.metaTitle: Epe Smoked Fish and Lagoon Lunch | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Follow the smoke to Epe. 7 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Kano's Indigo Pits
summary: The Kofar Mata dye pits in old Kano are stone-lined vats where cloth is soaked in indigo and beaten until it takes the colour. A dyer takes you through each step, and you can try wringing and pounding a piece of cotton yourself.

seo.metaTitle: Kano's Indigo Pits | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Cloth dyed the same way for 500 years. 5 hours small-group tour in Kano, Nigeria.

title: Gidan Makama and the Old City Wall
summary: Gidan Makama is a 15th-century palace turned museum, and the old city walls and gates are still partly standing around it. You walk the centre of the old city with a Kano-born guide who explains how the Hausa city-state traded across the Sahara.

seo.metaTitle: Gidan Makama and the Old City Wall | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A palace, a museum, a lot of mud brick. 4 hours small-group tour in Kano, Nigeria.

title: Kurmi Market and the Camel Road
summary: Kurmi is one of Africa's oldest markets, and traders there still sell leather, brass and hand-woven cloth the way their grandfathers did. Your guide takes you through the leather and calabash sections and sets up a conversation with a Hausa trader.

seo.metaTitle: Kurmi Market and the Camel Road | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Where the caravans used to end. 5 hours small-group tour in Kano, Nigeria.

title: Dala Hill Sunrise
summary: Dala Hill rises out of the city and is said to be where Kano's earliest settlers made their first homes. We climb at dawn, look down on the old walls and the Emir's palace, and come down to hot kosai and tea.

seo.metaTitle: Dala Hill Sunrise | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Climb the rock that Kano grew around. 3 hours small-group tour in Kano, Nigeria.

title: Calabar Carnival Backstage
summary: Every December Calabar turns into a street party, but the interesting part is the build-up. You visit a band's workshop, watch costume makers stitching sequins and feathers, and then join the street crowd when the groups come out. Dates vary, so book around December.

seo.metaTitle: Calabar Carnival Backstage | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Costumes before the parade. 8 hours small-group tour in Calabar, Nigeria.

title: Drill Ranch: The Apes Who Were Rescued
summary: Drill Ranch, run by the Pandrillus programme, looks after drills and chimpanzees confiscated from the bushmeat trade. A keeper takes you through the enclosures, explains how groups are rebuilt, and shows how the rescued animals are being prepared for release.

seo.metaTitle: Drill Ranch: The Apes Who Were Rescued | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Primate sanctuary run on a shoestring. 4 hours small-group tour in Calabar, Nigeria.

title: Kwa Falls and a River Swim
summary: Kwa Falls pours over several rock tiers into a pool in the Cross River forest. The walk in is short, the water is cool, and a local guide shows you where the current is safe. We have lunch back at the entrance.

seo.metaTitle: Kwa Falls and a River Swim | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A jungle cascade you can get into. 8 hours small-group tour in Calabar, Nigeria.

title: Mary Slessor's Calabar
summary: Mary Slessor spent decades in Calabar and the Cross River region, and her legacy is both admired and debated. We visit her grave, the old Duke Town church area and the Calabar Museum, with a historian guide who covers the missionary story and the slave trade that preceded it.

seo.metaTitle: Mary Slessor's Calabar | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A missionary**'**s story, told honestly. 5 hours small-group tour in Calabar, Nigeria.

title: Obudu Cable Car and Cloud Country
summary: Obudu Mountain Resort sits on a high plateau in Cross River State, with cool air, grassland and a cable car that climbs the escarpment. Over two days you ride up, walk the ranch trails, visit the canopy walkway, and take the guided hike along the escarpment edge.

seo.metaTitle: Obudu Cable Car and Cloud Country | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The plateau where it feels like Switzerland. 2 days small-group tour in Obudu, Nigeria.

title: Afi Mountain Gorilla Country
summary: Afi Mountain Wildlife Sanctuary protects Cross River gorillas, drills and chimpanzees. You hike with rangers, camp or stay in a nearby lodge, and learn about the community patrol programme that keeps hunters out.

seo.metaTitle: Afi Mountain Gorilla Country | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Rare apes, long hike, real forest. 2 days small-group tour in Cross River, Nigeria.

title: Ikom Monoliths: The Stones Nobody Can Explain
summary: Hundreds of carved stone monoliths stand in the villages around Ikom, some more than a thousand years old. A local historian takes you to several, explains the theories about who made them, and introduces you to the elders who look after them.

seo.metaTitle: Ikom Monoliths: The Stones Nobody Can Explain | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Carved heads in the Cross River bush. 7 hours small-group tour in Ikom, Nigeria.

title: Agbokim Waterfalls Picnic
summary: Agbokim is a cluster of cascades near the Cameroon border, with a viewing platform and a picnic area. We walk the trail to the main drop, cross the footbridge, and have lunch overlooking the falls.

seo.metaTitle: Agbokim Waterfalls Picnic | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Five falls, one cliff. 6 hours small-group tour in Cross River, Nigeria.

title: Jos Plateau: Cold Mornings in Nigeria
summary: The Jos Plateau sits high enough that mornings can be properly cold. We visit the Jos Wildlife Park, walk the rock formations, and have lunch in town with a guide from the Plateau who explains why farmers here grow potatoes and strawberries.

seo.metaTitle: Jos Plateau: Cold Mornings in Nigeria | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A cooler side of the country. 8 hours small-group tour in Jos, Nigeria.

title: Kurra Falls and Tin Mining Country
summary: The Jos area was Nigeria's tin capital until the mines went quiet. We visit Kurra Falls and drive through the old mining land, with commentary on how the industry shaped the Plateau.

seo.metaTitle: Kurra Falls and Tin Mining Country | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Waterfall in the middle of old mining land. 7 hours small-group tour in Jos, Nigeria.

title: Wase Rock and the Egrets
summary: Wase Rock rises out of the plains in northern Plateau State and is a nesting site for thousands of birds, including cattle egrets. You stay overnight in Wase town, climb a section of the rock at dawn, and watch the birds leave for the day.

seo.metaTitle: Wase Rock and the Egrets | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A giant granite thumb and thousands of birds. 2 days small-group tour in Wase, Nigeria.

title: Jos Museum Compound: Pots, Houses and Masks
summary: The Jos Museum compound includes a pottery museum and a museum of traditional Nigerian architecture, with full-scale replicas of Hausa, Igbo and Tiv houses. A curator guides you through, and you can spend time in the craft shop.

seo.metaTitle: Jos Museum Compound: Pots, Houses and Masks | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Three museums in one walk. 4 hours small-group tour in Jos, Nigeria.

title: Ibadan Rooftops from Bower Tower
summary: Ibadan's skyline is mostly corrugated iron roofs in orange and brown, and the best view is from Bower Tower on Oke Are hill. You climb the stairs, walk down through the old city, and stop at Cocoa House and Mapo Hall.

seo.metaTitle: Ibadan Rooftops from Bower Tower | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Rust-coloured city, all the way to the horizon. 4 hours small-group tour in Ibadan, Nigeria.

title: IITA Forest: Research Station and Rainforest
summary: The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture campus protects a patch of forest and farmland in the middle of Ibadan. A researcher walks you through plots of cassava, yam and cowpea and into the forest edge, where you look for birds and butterflies.

seo.metaTitle: IITA Forest: Research Station and Rainforest | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A forest hidden inside a research campus. 5 hours small-group tour in Ibadan, Nigeria.

title: Agodi Gardens Afternoon
summary: Agodi Gardens is a quiet leafy park with a lake, walkways and a small collection of animals. It works well for families and anyone who has spent too long in the city. Boat rides, picnics and a slow lunch are all built in.

seo.metaTitle: Agodi Gardens Afternoon | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Lakes, a mini zoo, and no agenda. 4 hours small-group tour in Ibadan, Nigeria.

title: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
summary: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove is a UNESCO site on the edge of Osogbo, filled with sculptures made by Susanne Wenger and followers of the Osun faith. A priestess or guide explains the shrines, the river and why the grove survived while others disappeared.

seo.metaTitle: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The forest that still has gods in it. 6 hours small-group tour in Osogbo, Nigeria.

title: Ife: The Bronze Heads and the Ooni's Court
summary: Ile-Ife is the spiritual home of the Yoruba, and its museum holds the famous bronze and terracotta heads. We visit the Ife Museum, the Ooni's palace gate and the Oranmiyan Staff, with a historian guide.

seo.metaTitle: Ife: The Bronze Heads and the Ooni's Court | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Where the Yoruba say the world began. 8 hours small-group tour in Ile-Ife, Nigeria.

title: Olumo Rock: Climb Abeokuta's Fortress
summary: Olumo Rock was a refuge during the 19th-century wars, and the people of Abeokuta still call it home. A guide takes you up through caves, past shrines and the old fig tree, to the top viewpoint, and tells you how the Egba used it as a fortress.

seo.metaTitle: Olumo Rock: Climb Abeokuta's Fortress | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The rock that sheltered a city. 6 hours small-group tour in Abeokuta, Nigeria.

title: Adire Day in Abeokuta
summary: Abeokuta is the home of adire, the Yoruba resist-dyed cloth. At the Itoku market area you watch dyers work in indigo and then make your own piece with cassava paste or tie-dye, which dries in the sun while we eat lunch.

seo.metaTitle: Adire Day in Abeokuta | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Resist-dye your own cloth. 6 hours small-group tour in Abeokuta, Nigeria.

title: Ikogosi: Where Hot and Cold Springs Meet
summary: At Ikogosi in Ekiti State a warm spring and a cold spring flow side by side and merge into one stream. You test the temperature difference, stay in the resort overnight, and walk the surrounding hills the next morning.

seo.metaTitle: Ikogosi: Where Hot and Cold Springs Meet | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Two streams, one confusing paddle. 2 days small-group tour in Ikogosi, Nigeria.

title: Idanre Hills: 660 Steps to the Old Town
summary: The ancient Idanre settlement, abandoned in the 1920s, sits at the top of the hill reached by 660 steps. You climb with a local guide, visit the old palace and the Owa's footprints, and sleep in town.

seo.metaTitle: Idanre Hills: 660 Steps to the Old Town | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A ghost town on top of a mountain. 2 days small-group tour in Idanre, Nigeria.

title: Erin-Ijesha: Seven Levels of Water
summary: Olumirin Waterfall in Erin-Ijesha tumbles down seven levels, and you can climb alongside it. A guide leads you up the steps and through the forest, and you cool off at the lower pool before lunch in the village.

seo.metaTitle: Erin-Ijesha: Seven Levels of Water | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Climb through the falls. 8 hours small-group tour in Erin-Ijesha, Nigeria.

title: Old Oyo National Park: Savannah and Ruins
summary: Old Oyo National Park holds the ruins of a former Yoruba capital among savannah and forest. You go on guided drives and walks, look for elephants and antelope, and learn about the empire that ruled this land.

seo.metaTitle: Old Oyo National Park: Savannah and Ruins | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Elephants, ruins and red dust. 2 days small-group tour in Oyo, Nigeria.

title: Ilorin Emirate: Sobi Hill and the Palace
summary: Ilorin sits where Yoruba and Hausa-Fulani cultures meet. You climb Sobi Hill for the view, visit the exterior of the Emir's palace and learn about the emirate's history, then eat at a local canteen.

seo.metaTitle: Ilorin Emirate: Sobi Hill and the Palace | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The northern edge of Yoruba land. 5 hours small-group tour in Ilorin, Nigeria.

title: Owu Falls: Kwara's Big Drop
summary: Owu Falls, in Kwara State, drops over a high cliff into a gorge and is one of the tallest falls in the country. You walk down for a view, camp or stay nearby, and spend the second day exploring the surrounding villages.

seo.metaTitle: Owu Falls: Kwara's Big Drop | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Rumoured to be Nigeria**'**s tallest. 2 days small-group tour in Kwara, Nigeria.

title: Nike Lake Weekend
summary: Enugu was a coal town, and it still has hills and rock faces that remind you. You stay by Nike Lake, take boat rides, walk the Ngwo Pine Forest and visit the coal mine museum.

seo.metaTitle: Nike Lake Weekend | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Lake, hills and coal-city streets. 2 days small-group tour in Enugu, Nigeria.

title: Ngwo Caves and Awhum Waterfall
summary: The Ngwo caves have long tunnels and rock chambers, and nearby Awhum Waterfall is tied to a monastery and a hill community. A guide leads you through both, stopping to explain what the locals believe about each.

seo.metaTitle: Ngwo Caves and Awhum Waterfall | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Underground and over the edge. 8 hours small-group tour in Enugu, Nigeria.

title: Ariaria: The Made-in-Aba Market
summary: Aba is Nigeria's best-known manufacturing hub for leather goods and fashion, and Ariaria market is its engine room. You walk through shoe workshops and tailoring lanes, meet makers and learn how Aba products reach the whole country.

seo.metaTitle: Ariaria: The Made-in-Aba Market | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Shoes, bags and a lot of clever copying. 6 hours small-group tour in Aba, Nigeria.

title: Onitsha Main Market and the Niger Bridge
summary: Onitsha has one of West Africa's biggest markets and a bridge that crosses the Niger. You spend a morning with a trader guide in the market, then walk to the river for views of the bridge and ferries.

seo.metaTitle: Onitsha Main Market and the Niger Bridge | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: River crossings and the world**'**s busiest stalls. 6 hours small-group tour in Onitsha, Nigeria.

title: Arochukwu: The Long Juju Caves
summary: The Aro people ran an oracle and trading network from this hilltop town, and the Long Juju cave is its most famous site. A historian guides you through the town, the caves and the old slave-trade story.

seo.metaTitle: Arochukwu: The Long Juju Caves | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Oracle country in Abia State. 2 days small-group tour in Arochukwu, Nigeria.

title: Umuahia War Museum Day
summary: The National War Museum in Umuahia holds weapons, vehicles and documents from the Nigerian civil war. A guide presents the history carefully and with respect for those who lived through it.

seo.metaTitle: Umuahia War Museum Day | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The Biafra story, from the museum. 4 hours small-group tour in Umuahia, Nigeria.

title: Benin Bronze Street
summary: Igun Street in Benin City is where families have cast bronze for generations. You watch lost-wax casting, visit the Benin Moat remains and the Oba's palace exterior, and hear why so many Benin bronzes ended up in foreign museums.

seo.metaTitle: Benin Bronze Street | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Casters at work in Igun. 5 hours small-group tour in Benin City, Nigeria.

title: Yankari Game Reserve: Warm Spring and Elephants
summary: Yankari is Nigeria's best-known game reserve, with elephants, baboons and the Wikki Warm Spring, where you can swim. Three days gives you guided drives, a ranger walk, and a dip in the clear water.

seo.metaTitle: Yankari Game Reserve: Warm Spring and Elephants | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Safari in Nigeria**'**s north-east. 3 days small-group tour in Yankari, Nigeria.

title: Mambilla Plateau: Tea Country
summary: The Mambilla Plateau in Taraba State is cool, green grazing and tea country, a very different Nigeria from the humid south. You visit a tea estate, ride across open grassland and stay in Gembu with local families who run cattle and grow potatoes.

seo.metaTitle: Mambilla Plateau: Tea Country | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Highland farms above the clouds. 3 days small-group tour in Mambilla, Nigeria.

title: Sukur: UNESCO Hilltop Kingdom
summary: The Sukur Cultural Landscape is a UNESCO site with a chief's palace, stone terraces and iron-working traditions. You hike up, meet the Hidi's family and see how the community still farms.

seo.metaTitle: Sukur: UNESCO Hilltop Kingdom | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Terraces and a palace, untouched. 3 days small-group tour in Adamawa, Nigeria.

title: Gashaka-Gumti: Nigeria's Wildest Park
summary: Gashaka-Gumti is Nigeria's largest national park, with mountains, savannah and forest running to the Cameroon border. You trek with rangers, sleep at a field station and look for chimpanzees, buffalo and hartebeest, with a village stop on the way in.

seo.metaTitle: Gashaka-Gumti: Nigeria's Wildest Park | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Chimps, buffaloes and no crowds. 4 days small-group tour in Taraba, Nigeria.

title: Katsina's Gobarau Minaret
summary: The Gobarau Minaret was once part of a major centre of learning in Hausaland. A local guide explains the history, takes you around the old city walls and the Emir's palace exterior.

seo.metaTitle: Katsina's Gobarau Minaret | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A tower that guided scholars. 5 hours small-group tour in Katsina, Nigeria.

title: Zaria: Palace and City Wall
summary: Zaria is one of the oldest Hausa cities. You tour the old palace exterior, walk the wall and visit a local weaver before a lunch of tuwo and miyan kuka.

seo.metaTitle: Zaria: Palace and City Wall | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: The emirate that outlasted empires. 5 hours small-group tour in Zaria, Nigeria.

title: Sokoto: The Caliphate City
summary: Sokoto was the capital of the Sokoto Caliphate, founded by Usman dan Fodio. You visit the Sultan's palace exterior, the tomb of dan Fodio and the old market.

seo.metaTitle: Sokoto: The Caliphate City | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A walk through Sokoto**'**s story. 6 hours small-group tour in Sokoto, Nigeria.

title: Lokoja: Where the Niger Meets the Benue
summary: Lokoja is the confluence city, where the brown Niger meets the green Benue. You climb Mount Patti for the view, visit Lord Lugard's old house and take a boat to the meeting point.

seo.metaTitle: Lokoja: Where the Niger Meets the Benue | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Two rivers, one view. 8 hours small-group tour in Lokoja, Nigeria.

title: Argungu Fishing Festival
summary: Every year in Kebbi State, fishermen race into the Matan Fada river with hand nets in a contest to catch the biggest fish. You attend the festival, see the durbar and stay with a local family. Dates change yearly.

seo.metaTitle: Argungu Fishing Festival | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Thousands of men, one pond, bare hands. 3 days small-group tour in Argungu, Nigeria.

title: Osun Festival Week
summary: Every August, followers of Osun gather at the grove in Osogbo for a pilgrimage with processions, offerings and drumming. We time the tour with the festival and arrange respectful viewing spots.

seo.metaTitle: Osun Festival Week | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A pilgrimage, not a parade. 3 days small-group tour in Osogbo, Nigeria.

title: Port Harcourt Creek Run
summary: Port Harcourt sits in the Niger Delta, and a boat trip through the creeks shows the mangroves and fishing communities alongside the oil industry. A local guide explains both sides.

seo.metaTitle: Port Harcourt Creek Run | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Mangroves and oil city contradictions. 6 hours small-group tour in Port Harcourt, Nigeria.

title: Ibeno Beach: West Africa's Long Sand
summary: Ibeno is a long Atlantic beach in Akwa Ibom State, lined with fishing boats. You walk the shoreline, watch the catch come in and eat grilled fish on the sand.

seo.metaTitle: Ibeno Beach: West Africa's Long Sand | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Fishing boats and endless shoreline. 2 days small-group tour in Akwa Ibom, Nigeria.

title: Ilashe Beach Day
summary: Ilashe is reached by a short boat ride from Lagos and feels like a different country. Sandy shore, quiet water and a long lunch with palm trees overhead.

seo.metaTitle: Ilashe Beach Day | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Boat out, eat well, stay all day. 8 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Argungu to Kebbi: Fish Smoking and Rice
summary: Kebbi State is known for rice and fish. You visit rice farms, a fish-smoking village on the river and eat in a family compound, with a guide translating the conversation and explaining the harvest calendar.

seo.metaTitle: Argungu to Kebbi: Fish Smoking and Rice | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Kebbi**'**s riverside food. 2 days small-group tour in Kebbi, Nigeria.

title: Calabar After Dark: Masks, Drums and Street Food
summary: In Calabar, the Ekpe society still has a role in cultural life. A knowledgeable guide explains what you may and may not see, then you walk the Marina area and eat street food.

seo.metaTitle: Calabar After Dark: Masks, Drums and Street Food | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Where the old societies still matter. 5 hours small-group tour in Calabar, Nigeria.

title: Cross River Rainforest Trek
summary: Cross River National Park protects some of the last intact rainforest in Nigeria. You trek with rangers, camp under the canopy and visit a village at the park's edge, where you hear about the community patrol work.

seo.metaTitle: Cross River Rainforest Trek | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A forest where leopards still live. 3 days small-group tour in Cross River, Nigeria.

title: Lagos Tin Can Island at Night
summary: Lagos Port is one of the busiest in West Africa. From a boat at dusk you watch the ships queue and the cranes light up, with commentary from a guide who knows the port's history.

seo.metaTitle: Lagos Tin Can Island at Night | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Container ships and harbour lights. 3 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Oba's Market Morning in Benin
summary: Benin's markets sell coral beads, brass jewellery and cloth, items long associated with the Oba's court. A guide shows you how to spot real coral and where to buy brass at fair prices.

seo.metaTitle: Oba's Market Morning in Benin | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Beads, brass and breakfast. 4 hours small-group tour in Benin City, Nigeria.

title: Ogoja and Cross River Hills
summary: Ogoja is hilly, green and little visited. You hike farm ridges with a local farmer, stay in a family home and visit the Saturday market, where traders bring yams, palm oil and bush mango.

seo.metaTitle: Ogoja and Cross River Hills | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Valleys and footpaths in the north. 2 days small-group tour in Ogoja, Nigeria.

title: Nsukka and the Odinani Museum
summary: Nsukka is home to a university art school and the Odinani museum, which displays Igbo religion, art and ritual. A local curator guides you and a potter shows how clay is shaped.

seo.metaTitle: Nsukka and the Odinani Museum | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Igbo art, mask and clay. 5 hours small-group tour in Nsukka, Nigeria.

title: Olosunta Hill: Ikere's Own Mountain
summary: Olosunta Hill looms over Ikere-Ekiti and is tied up with local belief as well as local pride. A town guide leads the climb, points out the shrine sites, and the top gives a wide view over the farmland.

seo.metaTitle: Olosunta Hill: Ikere's Own Mountain | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A short, steep morning hike. 5 hours small-group tour in Ikere-Ekiti, Nigeria.

title: Kainji Lake: Boats, Fish and Birds
summary: Kainji Lake is a giant reservoir on the Niger, with a national park on its shores. A boat takes you across the water to fishing communities and hippo pools, with a ranger identifying birds along the way.

seo.metaTitle: Kainji Lake: Boats, Fish and Birds | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: A huge reservoir, barely known. 2 days small-group tour in Kainji, Nigeria.

title: Night Stalls of Lagos
summary: After dark, Lagos markets change character. A guide takes you through night stalls, music corners and food stands in well-lit areas, tasting roasted corn, suya and fried plantain as the traffic thins.

seo.metaTitle: Night Stalls of Lagos | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Late shopping and louder music. 3 hours small-group tour in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: Ife to Ilesa: Gold and Greenery
summary: Between Ife and Ilesa you pass cocoa farms, old palaces and artisan villages. You stop at a cocoa farm to taste fresh pods, visit the Owa's palace and stay in Ilesa.

seo.metaTitle: Ife to Ilesa: Gold and Greenery | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Cocoa belt road trip. 2 days small-group tour in Osun, Nigeria.

title: Jebba and the Niger Gorge
summary: At Jebba the Niger squeezes through a rocky gorge crossed by a railway bridge and a hydro dam. You walk the banks, watch fishermen cast nets from canoes and photograph the old bridge from the water.

seo.metaTitle: Jebba and the Niger Gorge | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Rapids and a railway bridge. 5 hours small-group tour in Jebba, Nigeria.

title: Assop Falls and Shere Hills
summary: Assop Falls tumbles over a rock ledge in a wooded valley outside Jos, and Shere Hills gives the high view over the city. We hike a short section of Shere in the morning, swim at Assop if the water is right, and have lunch in a Plateau village.

seo.metaTitle: Assop Falls and Shere Hills | Nigeria
seo.metaDescription: Two Plateau classics in one day. 8 hours small-group tour in Jos, Nigeria.

title: Kente Cloth, Start to Finish at Bonwire
summary: Bonwire is the village most people credit with putting kente on the world map. Weavers here work narrow strips on wooden looms, and each pattern has a name and a meaning. You watch the process, try a few passes on a loom yourself, and learn why a wedding cloth differs from a funeral one.

seo.metaTitle: Kente Cloth, Start to Finish at Bonwire | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Sit at the loom and lose an hour. 6 hours small-group tour in Bonwire, Ghana.

title: Adinkra Stamps and Black Dye at Ntonso
summary: In Ntonso, cloth is stamped with carved calabash blocks dipped in dye made from tree bark and iron slag. Each symbol has its own saying. You make your own piece, wait for it to dry in the sun and take it away.

seo.metaTitle: Adinkra Stamps and Black Dye at Ntonso | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Symbols you can carry home. 5 hours small-group tour in Ntonso, Ghana.

title: Kejetia After Lunch: Inside West Africa's Biggest Market
summary: Kejetia is a maze of stalls and covered lanes, and a first-time visitor can lose an afternoon. Your guide has traders they've known for years, so you get to stop and talk instead of being herded. You buy a few things properly, with prices explained.

seo.metaTitle: Kejetia After Lunch: Inside West Africa's Biggest Market | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Eight thousand stalls, one patient guide. 4 hours small-group tour in Kumasi, Ghana.

title: Manhyia Palace and Asante Gold Weights
summary: The Manhyia Palace Museum tells the story of the Asante kings through regalia, portraits and the small brass gold weights once used for trade. A guide explains how the proverbs behind the weights worked as a code of conduct.

seo.metaTitle: Manhyia Palace and Asante Gold Weights | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A palace museum with a crowd of tiny brass figures. 4 hours small-group tour in Kumasi, Ghana.

title: Okomfo Anokye's Sword in the Road
summary: At Adum, in central Kumasi, a sword stands lodged in rock. The story says the priest Okomfo Anokye drove it in to bind the Asante together, and that the kingdom falls if it is ever pulled out. We visit the site and walk a short route through Asante history.

seo.metaTitle: Okomfo Anokye's Sword in the Road | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A legend you can walk up to. 3 hours small-group tour in Kumasi, Ghana.

title: Ahwiaa Woodcarvers: Stools, Drums and Splinters
summary: Ahwiaa is where Kumasi's stool carvers work, hacking Asante stools out of single blocks of wood with adzes and finishing them with a hot iron. A master carver talks you through the symbols on the seat supports, then lets you carve a small spoon or drum peg yourself.

seo.metaTitle: Ahwiaa Woodcarvers: Stools, Drums and Splinters | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Carve a stool leg, or try. 5 hours small-group tour in Ahwiaa, Ghana.

title: Lake Bosumtwi: The Crater Lake
summary: Lake Bosumtwi fills a meteor crater and is sacred to the Asante, who say the souls of the dead go there to say goodbye to the god Twi. Fishermen paddle out on wooden planks called padua. You swim, take a boat and eat tilapia by the lake.

seo.metaTitle: Lake Bosumtwi: The Crater Lake | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A swim in a meteor hole. 9 hours small-group tour in Lake Bosumtwi, Ghana.

title: Adanwomase: The Quiet Kente Village
summary: Adanwomase is the quieter rival to Bonwire, and weavers there often work in silk on narrow looms under open sheds. They are happy to explain why certain patterns belong to chiefs, and you can order a strip woven to your own colours and collect it later.

seo.metaTitle: Adanwomase: The Quiet Kente Village | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Silk, not tourists. 5 hours small-group tour in Adanwomase, Ghana.

title: Mole at Dawn: Walk with Elephants
summary: Mole is Ghana's largest wildlife park, and the walking safaris are among the best in West Africa. Over three days you track elephants on foot, see antelope and baboons, and watch the sun rise over the waterhole from the motel terrace.

seo.metaTitle: Mole at Dawn: Walk with Elephants | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: On foot, with a ranger. 3 days small-group tour in Mole National Park, Ghana.

title: Larabanga: The Mud Mosque
summary: Larabanga's mosque is built in the Sudanese style with mud and wooden poles, and is thought to date back to the 1400s. A village guide explains its history and the legend of the Holy Quran said to have fallen from the sky.

seo.metaTitle: Larabanga: The Mud Mosque | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: West Africa**'**s oldest, they say. 4 hours small-group tour in Larabanga, Ghana.

title: Mognori: A Village With Rules
summary: Mognori is a village near Mole run on community rules: farmers agree where cattle can graze and where wildlife stays undisturbed. You paddle a dugout on the river at dawn, watch for birds and monkeys, then sit with the chief's family for a lunch of tuo zaafi and green soup.

seo.metaTitle: Mognori: A Village With Rules | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Canoes, hippos and a chief**'**s welcome. 2 days small-group tour in Mognori, Ghana.

title: Paga Crocodile Pond: Touch the Sacred Reptile
summary: At Paga, crocodiles are treated as ancestors, and the ponds are shared with villagers who bring chickens to call them. A local guide explains the taboos, then walks you to the Pikworo Slave Camp to see the stone bowls and sleeping rocks used by captives.

seo.metaTitle: Paga Crocodile Pond: Touch the Sacred Reptile | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Chickens, crocs and local etiquette. 5 hours small-group tour in Paga, Ghana.

title: Sirigu: Wall Paintings and Clay Pots
summary: The Kassena women of Sirigu repaint their compound walls with black, red and white geometric patterns after each rainy season, and they make clay pots in the same designs. You join the women at the pottery shed and learn why each shape and symbol is used.

seo.metaTitle: Sirigu: Wall Paintings and Clay Pots | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Women**'**s art on mud walls. 6 hours small-group tour in Sirigu, Ghana.

title: Bolga Baskets in the Making
summary: Bolga baskets begin as elephant grass cut in the dry season, dyed, and coiled tightly around a core. At a weavers' compound outside Bolgatanga you watch the process, try a few rows yourself and buy directly from the weaver, with fair-price tips from the guide.

seo.metaTitle: Bolga Baskets in the Making | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: From grass to market tote. 5 hours small-group tour in Bolgatanga, Ghana.

title: Tengzug Shrine and the Talensi Hills
summary: The Tengzug shrine sits among huge boulders in the Talensi hills, and the Talensi people have visited it for generations. Your guide explains shoe, camera and clothing rules, then leads a walk up the rocks with views across the plains.

seo.metaTitle: Tengzug Shrine and the Talensi Hills | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Boulders, shrines and a long view. 7 hours small-group tour in Tongo, Ghana.

title: Navrongo Cathedral: Mud Walls and Painted Patterns
summary: Navrongo Cathedral is built from mud and decorated in the same patterns the Kassena paint on their homes. The priest or a parish guide explains how local artists shaped the interior, and the lunch afterwards is rice balls and groundnut soup in town.

seo.metaTitle: Navrongo Cathedral: Mud Walls and Painted Patterns | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A church the colour of the ground. 4 hours small-group tour in Navrongo, Ghana.

title: Tamale Smock Weavers and the Damba
summary: Tamale is Dagomba country, and its central market sells everything from smocks to shea butter. You watch a weaver work a narrow loom, see the northern smock made up, and learn the stories behind the Damba festival processions.

seo.metaTitle: Tamale Smock Weavers and the Damba | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Cloth, drums and chiefs. 6 hours small-group tour in Tamale, Ghana.

title: Salaga: The Market That Sold People
summary: Salaga was a major inland slave market in the 19th century, and a historian walks you through the market square and the wells where captives were held. The tour is quiet, unhurried and honest, with time to sit and ask questions.

seo.metaTitle: Salaga: The Market That Sold People | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A hard history, carefully told. 8 hours small-group tour in Salaga, Ghana.

title: Wli Falls: The Tallest in West Africa
summary: Wli Falls cascades from a height of over 80 metres in Volta Region. The walk through forest takes about 45 minutes, and the lower falls have a swimmable pool. You stay overnight in a nearby village.

seo.metaTitle: Wli Falls: The Tallest in West Africa | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A forest hike to a two-tier drop. 2 days small-group tour in Wli, Ghana.

title: Mount Afadjato: Climb Ghana's Highest
summary: At 885 metres, Afadjato is Ghana's highest point and the climb is short but steep. A guide from Liate Wote village leads you through forest to the summit, where Togo is visible on a clear day.

seo.metaTitle: Mount Afadjato: Climb Ghana's Highest | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: 885 metres of green. 8 hours small-group tour in Afadjato, Ghana.

title: Tafi Atome: The Monkeys Who Live in the Village
summary: In Tafi Atome the mona monkeys are protected by village custom. A community guide leads you into the sacred forest, where bananas coax the monkeys down to eye level, and you hear how the village's rules began.

seo.metaTitle: Tafi Atome: The Monkeys Who Live in the Village | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Mona monkeys that follow the rules. 5 hours small-group tour in Tafi Atome, Ghana.

title: Akosombo and the Man-Made Sea
summary: Akosombo's dam created one of the world's largest man-made lakes, displacing many villages. A guide walks you across the dam, explains the power story and takes you to the Adomi Bridge for river views.

seo.metaTitle: Akosombo and the Man-Made Sea | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Dam, lake and a very big boat. 8 hours small-group tour in Akosombo, Ghana.

title: Ada Foah: Where River Meets Ocean
summary: At Ada Foah the Volta River slows and spreads before meeting the sea. A boat takes you through the estuary to a sandbar, past fishing canoes and mangrove islands, with a lunch of grilled tilapia at a riverside shack.

seo.metaTitle: Ada Foah: Where River Meets Ocean | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Sandbars, dolphins and a guesthouse. 2 days small-group tour in Ada Foah, Ghana.

title: Keta Lagoon and the Sea Wall
summary: Keta sits on a thin strip of land between lagoon and sea, and the sea has taken many streets over the years. A guide shows the concrete sea defences, a fishermen's quarter and the lagoon from a canoe.

seo.metaTitle: Keta Lagoon and the Sea Wall | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Land with water on both sides. 2 days small-group tour in Keta, Ghana.

title: Songor Salt Harvest
summary: At the Songor Lagoon, women rake and carry salt in the dry season, working in the heat for hours. You join a harvest for an hour, taste the fresh crust and hear how the trade is organised.

seo.metaTitle: Songor Salt Harvest | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: White crust under hot sun. 5 hours small-group tour in Ada, Ghana.

title: Nzulezo: The Village on Stilts
summary: Nzulezo is a UNESCO-listed village built entirely on stilts over Lake Tadane. You paddle in through a channel lined with raffia palms, walk the plank paths between houses and meet a family who have lived on the water for generations.

seo.metaTitle: Nzulezo: The Village on Stilts | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A boat ride into the swamp. 2 days small-group tour in Beyin, Ghana.

title: Busua Beach Surf and Fish
summary: Busua's bay breaks small, steady waves that suit beginners, and the sand is soft enough to forgive early falls. A local instructor handles the foam-board lesson, then you eat grilled snapper with pepper sauce and fried yam at a beach shack before the afternoon tide changes.

seo.metaTitle: Busua Beach Surf and Fish | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Learn on a longboard, eat grilled snapper. 8 hours small-group tour in Busua, Ghana.

title: Cape Three Points: Ghana's Southern Tip
summary: Cape Three Points is where Ghana's coast turns east. A guide walks the headland, shows the lighthouse and takes you through small villages where fishing boats are drawn up on the sand.

seo.metaTitle: Cape Three Points: Ghana's Southern Tip | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A lighthouse at the very end. 8 hours small-group tour in Cape Three Points, Ghana.

title: Ankasa Forest: Trails Few People Walk
summary: Ankasa is one of Ghana's wettest and wildest forests, with few visitors. You walk with a ranger, listen for hornbills and monkeys, and sleep at a basic camp with solar lights.

seo.metaTitle: Ankasa Forest: Trails Few People Walk | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Real rainforest, real mud. 3 days small-group tour in Ankasa, Ghana.

title: Kakum Canopy at Eight in the Morning
summary: The Kakum canopy walk is a series of rope bridges 30 metres above the forest floor. Going early means cool air, forest noise and thin crowds; a guide then leads a ground-level nature walk.

seo.metaTitle: Kakum Canopy at Eight in the Morning | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Seven bridges, one tall tree. 6 hours small-group tour in Kakum, Ghana.

title: Hans Cottage Botel: Crocodiles with Your Fish
summary: Hans Cottage Botel sits beside a lagoon filled with crocodiles. A raised walkway lets you watch them from above, and lunch is tilapia or chicken with banku on the terrace.

seo.metaTitle: Hans Cottage Botel: Crocodiles with Your Fish | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A moat-side lunch. 3 hours small-group tour in Cape Coast, Ghana.

title: Assin Manso: The Ancestral Slave River
summary: Assin Manso was a staging point on the slave route, and the Donkor Nsuo river is where captives bathed before the march to the coast. A guide leads the visit with care and time for reflection.

seo.metaTitle: Assin Manso: The Ancestral Slave River | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A memorial and a river. 5 hours small-group tour in Assin Manso, Ghana.

title: Aburi Gardens and the Craft Village
summary: Aburi sits in the cooler Akuapem hills, and its botanical gardens have giant trees, orchids and a shaded teahouse. The craft village nearby sells carved masks and furniture, and carvers will show you how a block of wood becomes a figure.

seo.metaTitle: Aburi Gardens and the Craft Village | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Botanical garden plus woodcarvers. 6 hours small-group tour in Aburi, Ghana.

title: Boti Falls and the Umbrella Rock
summary: Boti Falls is a twin cascade in the Eastern Region, and the walk includes a rock formation known as Umbrella Rock. A local guide leads a short hike down to the pool.

seo.metaTitle: Boti Falls and the Umbrella Rock | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A waterfall with a strange neighbour. 8 hours small-group tour in Boti, Ghana.

title: Krobo Beads: Glass Melted in Clay
summary: Krobo bead-makers crush old glass into powder, pack it in clay moulds and fire it until it fuses. At Odumase-Krobo you watch the process, make a bead and learn what colours and patterns signify.

seo.metaTitle: Krobo Beads: Glass Melted in Clay | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Pour, roll, fire, repeat. 6 hours small-group tour in Odumase-Krobo, Ghana.

title: Kwahu Plateau: Paragliding over the Hills
summary: Along the Kwahu escarpment, pilots launch from a ridge above the valley, mostly around Easter when the festival crowds arrive. You run a few steps strapped to a tandem pilot, lift off, and drift over farms and roads before landing in a field. Winds decide the day.

seo.metaTitle: Kwahu Plateau: Paragliding over the Hills | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Run off a ridge on purpose. 6 hours small-group tour in Kwahu, Ghana.

title: Bunso Arboretum: Trees and Canopy Bridges
summary: Bunso sits above the Accra–Kumasi road, a patch of managed forest with labelled trees and a short canopy bridge. A guide points out which trees were once logged, how birds use the layers, and where to find butterflies along the stream trail.

seo.metaTitle: Bunso Arboretum: Trees and Canopy Bridges | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A forest walk out of Accra. 8 hours small-group tour in Bunso, Ghana.

title: Boabeng-Fiema: Monkeys by Agreement
summary: The villages of Boabeng and Fiema have protected their monkeys for generations. A guide leads you to black-and-white colobus and mona monkeys, and explains the local taboo against harming them.

seo.metaTitle: Boabeng-Fiema: Monkeys by Agreement | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Colobus and mona, protected by custom. 2 days small-group tour in Boabeng-Fiema, Ghana.

title: Kintampo Waterfalls: Falls at the Centre
summary: Kintampo's waterfalls spread across broad stone steps rather than one big drop, so you can wade in and sit under small cascades. The walk is easy, and a village stall at the entrance sells fried yam and groundnuts for a lazy lunch.

seo.metaTitle: Kintampo Waterfalls: Falls at the Centre | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Ghana**'**s halfway point. 6 hours small-group tour in Kintampo, Ghana.

title: Techiman Market: Maize Mountains
summary: Techiman is one of the biggest food markets in the country, piled with yam, maize, onions and tomatoes. A guide helps you navigate and find lunch in a market canteen.

seo.metaTitle: Techiman Market: Maize Mountains | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A food market, not a tourist one. 5 hours small-group tour in Techiman, Ghana.

title: Teshie Fantasy Coffins
summary: Teshie's carpenters build coffins shaped like what a person loved or did: a fishing boat for a fisherman, a Mercedes for a driver, an onion for a trader. A master carpenter shows the workshop, explains how the tradition began in the 1950s, and lets you sand a piece.

seo.metaTitle: Teshie Fantasy Coffins | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Buried in a fish, a Mercedes or a shoe. 4 hours small-group tour in Teshie, Ghana.

title: W.E.B. Du Bois Centre: A Quiet House in Accra
summary: W.E.B. Du Bois spent his final years in Ghana and is buried in the garden of his Accra house. A guide connects his life to the Pan-African movement, and you can see his study and library.

seo.metaTitle: W.E.B. Du Bois Centre: A Quiet House in Accra | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: The scholar who chose Ghana. 3 hours small-group tour in Accra, Ghana.

title: Labadi Beach on Horseback
summary: Labadi's sand is broad and flat at low tide, which suits a slow horse ride. Handlers match you to a horse, lead you along the waterline and stop for photos. Afterwards you sit with kelewele, the spiced fried plantain sold at beach stalls, and watch the afternoon crowds.

seo.metaTitle: Labadi Beach on Horseback | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Ride the shoreline. 3 hours small-group tour in Accra, Ghana.

title: Bojo Beach: The Lagoon Day Out
summary: Bojo sits on a sandbar across a lagoon, reached by a short canoe ride from the main road. The beach is quiet during the week, with palms for shade and a small restaurant serving grilled tilapia and banku. Swim, nap, and watch the canoes ferry people across.

seo.metaTitle: Bojo Beach: The Lagoon Day Out | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Cross the water to a sandspit. 8 hours small-group tour in Accra, Ghana.

title: Shai Hills: Baboons and Rock Caves
summary: Shai Hills is a short drive from Accra and feels far from it. A ranger walks you past baboon troops, through savannah grass to rocky outcrops, and into caves once used as shelters. Bring water and a hat; there's little shade.

seo.metaTitle: Shai Hills: Baboons and Rock Caves | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: An hour from Accra and wild. 6 hours small-group tour in Shai Hills, Ghana.

title: Kokrobite Drums and Beach
summary: Kokrobite's beach bars host drumming nights, but the better experience is a daytime lesson with a local drummer. You learn three basic djembe rhythms, hear what each one is used for at funerals and festivals, then eat fried fish and chips on the sand.

seo.metaTitle: Kokrobite Drums and Beach | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Hands on the drum, feet in the sand. 5 hours small-group tour in Kokrobite, Ghana.

title: Winneba Aboakyer: The Deer Hunt Festival
summary: The Aboakyer Festival is held in Winneba each May, and two teams of the Effutu people compete to catch a live deer. You join the day with a local guide, stay overnight and eat with a family.

seo.metaTitle: Winneba Aboakyer: The Deer Hunt Festival | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Teams race to catch a deer. 2 days small-group tour in Winneba, Ghana.

title: Ho and the Adaklu Hills
summary: Ho is the Volta Region's capital and a good base for hill walks. You climb Mount Adaklu with a guide who farms on its slopes, visit kente weavers in a nearby compound and learn how Ewe traditions differ from Asante ones.

seo.metaTitle: Ho and the Adaklu Hills | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Hills with a view over Volta. 2 days small-group tour in Ho, Ghana.

title: Amedzofe: The Village in the Clouds
summary: Amedzofe sits high in the Volta hills, where mornings are cool enough for a jacket. You hike to Tagbo Falls, pass farm plots and a mission church built by German missionaries, and eat lunch in a family home with a view over the valley.

seo.metaTitle: Amedzofe: The Village in the Clouds | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Fresh air, 5 hours of hills. 2 days small-group tour in Amedzofe, Ghana.

title: Kpetoe and Agbozume: Ewe Kente Country
summary: Ewe kente is woven in a different style from Asante kente, often with bold colours and pictorial motifs. You visit weavers in Kpetoe and learn to tell the two traditions apart.

seo.metaTitle: Kpetoe and Agbozume: Ewe Kente Country | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Different patterns, different colours. 6 hours small-group tour in Kpetoe, Ghana.

title: Axim Beach and the Lagoon
summary: Axim is a quiet coastal town where fishermen still launch from the beach each morning. You paddle a canoe through the lagoon, watch nets being mended and eat grilled fish on a plastic table by the water.

seo.metaTitle: Axim Beach and the Lagoon | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Lazy day on the coast. 8 hours small-group tour in Axim, Ghana.

title: Takoradi Market Circle
summary: Market Circle is Takoradi's busiest corner, a ring of cloth stalls, spice sellers and food stands. A local guide helps you find real wax print, shows you how to bargain without offending anyone and picks a stall for a quick plate of red-red.

seo.metaTitle: Takoradi Market Circle | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Fabric, fish and pure noise. 4 hours small-group tour in Takoradi, Ghana.

title: Sekondi Railway Museum
summary: Sekondi was the base of Ghana's colonial railway, and the museum holds locomotives, tickets and maps. A former railway worker or museum guide tells how the line carried gold, cocoa and timber to the coast, and how workers' strikes shaped the town.

seo.metaTitle: Sekondi Railway Museum | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Steam and old steel. 3 hours small-group tour in Sekondi, Ghana.

title: Tamale to Yendi: A Dagomba Road Trip
summary: Yendi is the traditional seat of the Dagomba kingdom. The drive from Tamale passes small villages, and in Yendi you see the exterior of the Ya-Na's palace, meet a local elder and eat lunch with a family.

seo.metaTitle: Tamale to Yendi: A Dagomba Road Trip | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: The old kingdom, from the car. 2 days small-group tour in Yendi, Ghana.

title: Gambaga Escarpment Sunrise
summary: The Gambaga Escarpment runs like a long wall across northern Ghana. You hike up before sunrise, watch the sun light the plains, and come down to a village breakfast of koko and bean cakes.

seo.metaTitle: Gambaga Escarpment Sunrise | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: The long ridge in the north. 6 hours small-group tour in Gambaga, Ghana.

title: Nalerigu: The Mamprusi Capital
summary: Nalerigu is the capital of the Mamprusi kingdom and home to the Nayiri's palace. A local historian walks you through the old town, explains how Mamprusi and Dagomba histories overlap and takes you up the escarpment for a view.

seo.metaTitle: Nalerigu: The Mamprusi Capital | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A palace and a hill. 5 hours small-group tour in Nalerigu, Ghana.

title: Kumasi Zoo and the Cultural Centre
summary: The Kumasi Centre for National Culture has craft stalls, a small museum and working artisans. The Kumasi Zoo is nearby, so this works well for families who want a slow morning with a bit of everything.

seo.metaTitle: Kumasi Zoo and the Cultural Centre | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Craft stalls and hornbills. 4 hours small-group tour in Kumasi, Ghana.

title: Elubo and the Cocoa Belt
summary: Cocoa farms in western Ghana look like tangled forest until you spot the pods growing straight from the trunks. A farmer shows how pods are cut, beans fermented and dried, and you taste the sweet white pulp before making a small chocolate bar.

seo.metaTitle: Elubo and the Cocoa Belt | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Cocoa from tree to bar. 2 days small-group tour in Western Region, Ghana.

title: Tema Fishing Harbour at Sunrise
summary: Tema's fishing harbour is crowded with painted canoes at dawn. You watch the catch come in, see women bargain for fish, and then follow some of it to a smoking shed, where the smell is as strong as the story.

seo.metaTitle: Tema Fishing Harbour at Sunrise | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Boats in, fish out. 3 hours small-group tour in Tema, Ghana.

title: Mount Gemi and Kpando
summary: Kpando sits on the Lake Volta shore, and the hill behind it climbs through farm plots to a view across the water. A local guide leads you up and brings you down to a lakeside restaurant for tilapia.

seo.metaTitle: Mount Gemi and Kpando | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A hill above Lake Volta. 6 hours small-group tour in Kpando, Ghana.

title: Daboya Smocks and Dye
summary: Daboya's cloth is dyed in deep indigo in earthen pits, then beaten with sticks. You visit the dye pits, watch the beating and see how smocks are sewn for northern chiefs. Overnight stays in town can be arranged.

seo.metaTitle: Daboya Smocks and Dye | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A northern town**'**s dyed cloth. 2 days small-group tour in Daboya, Ghana.

title: Cape Coast Fishing Village at Dawn
summary: Cape Coast's fishing beach is a working harbour of painted canoes, nets and noise. You arrive at dawn, watch boats land the catch and talk with fishermen about the changing seasons, then have fried fish for breakfast.

seo.metaTitle: Cape Coast Fishing Village at Dawn | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Colour, ropes and noise. 3 hours small-group tour in Cape Coast, Ghana.

title: Lake Volta Sunset Cruise
summary: A slow cruise on Lake Volta in the late afternoon, with tea and snacks on board. The boat drifts past fishing villages as the sky turns orange, and the captain explains how the lake rose when the dam was built.

seo.metaTitle: Lake Volta Sunset Cruise | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Slow boat, big sky. 3 hours small-group tour in Akosombo, Ghana.

title: Dodi Island Ferry Day
summary: Dodi Island sits in the Volta Lake and is reached by ferry. The community fishes, grows maize and sells smoked fish at a small market. A local host walks you around the island and explains how daily life changed after the lake formed.

seo.metaTitle: Dodi Island Ferry Day | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Cross Lake Volta to a village on an island. 6 hours small-group tour in Akosombo, Ghana.

title: Yaa Asantewaa Museum: The Woman Who Led a War
summary: Yaa Asantewaa led the Asante against British forces in 1900 over the Golden Stool. The museum at Ejisu holds her items and a guide explains the war, the exile that followed and why she is remembered.

seo.metaTitle: Yaa Asantewaa Museum: The Woman Who Led a War | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Ejisu and the golden stool story. 4 hours small-group tour in Ejisu, Ghana.

title: Kumasi Fort and the Military Museum
summary: The Kumasi Fort was built by the British after the Asante wars and now holds a military museum. A guide connects the exhibits to Asante resistance and the later colonial period.

seo.metaTitle: Kumasi Fort and the Military Museum | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Colonial stone, local stories. 3 hours small-group tour in Kumasi, Ghana.

title: National Museum Accra: Ten Thousand Years in Two Floors
summary: The Ghana National Museum in Accra holds pottery, masks and royal items spanning thousands of years. A museum guide skips the filler and takes you to the pieces that matter.

seo.metaTitle: National Museum Accra: Ten Thousand Years in Two Floors | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Archaeology, masks and a surprise or two. 3 hours small-group tour in Accra, Ghana.

title: Akropong Ridge: Basel Mission and the Akuapem Hills
summary: Akropong sits on the Akuapem Ridge, where Basel missionaries set up one of Ghana's first schools. You visit the old mission buildings and the Akuapem Museum, then drive the ridge road for the views.

seo.metaTitle: Akropong Ridge: Basel Mission and the Akuapem Hills | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Missionary houses on a green ridge. 6 hours small-group tour in Akropong, Ghana.

title: Wa Naa's Palace: Mud Architecture in Upper West
summary: Wa has one of the few surviving Sudanese-style palaces in Ghana, with mud walls and wooden beams. A guide explains the Wala kingdom and the building technique, and a local lunch follows.

seo.metaTitle: Wa Naa's Palace: Mud Architecture in Upper West | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Sudanese style in the north-west. 5 hours small-group tour in Wa, Ghana.

title: Wechiau Hippo Sanctuary by Canoe
summary: The Wechiau Community Hippo Sanctuary on the Black Volta is run by local villagers. You paddle a canoe with a guide, look for hippos and sleep in a nearby village.

seo.metaTitle: Wechiau Hippo Sanctuary by Canoe | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Paddle among the hippos. 2 days small-group tour in Wechiau, Ghana.

title: Sunday Best in Accra: Church, Cloth and Kenkey
summary: Sunday morning in Accra means church, with elaborate outfits and singing. A local host takes you to a welcoming congregation, then to a family lunch of kenkey and fried fish.

seo.metaTitle: Sunday Best in Accra: Church, Cloth and Kenkey | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Hats, hymns and a long lunch. 5 hours small-group tour in Accra, Ghana.

title: Krofofrom Brass Casters
summary: Krofofrom brass casters make gold weights and ornaments using lost-wax casting. A caster shows how a wax model is wrapped in clay, heated and filled with molten brass, then cracked open to reveal the shape. You can buy a piece directly from the maker.

seo.metaTitle: Krofofrom Brass Casters | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Lost-wax casting by the roadside. 5 hours small-group tour in Krofofrom, Ghana.

title: Bui Gorge: Hippos Below the Dam
summary: Bui National Park sits around the Black Volta near the Bui Dam. A boat takes you upriver to look for hippos, crocodiles and fish eagles, and a ranger walks you through the savannah woodland on the bank.

seo.metaTitle: Bui Gorge: Hippos Below the Dam | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: A river boat near a big dam. 2 days small-group tour in Bui, Ghana.

title: Atewa Range Birdwalk
summary: The Atewa Range is a cloud forest ridge with rare birds and butterflies. A local birder walks you along quiet trails at dawn and explains the debate around bauxite mining that threatens the range.

seo.metaTitle: Atewa Range Birdwalk | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Cloud forest on the edge of Accra**'**s reach. 6 hours small-group tour in Atewa, Ghana.

title: Akwidaa Turtle Watch
summary: Turtles nest on Akwidaa Beach in the Western Region in the late year. A community group runs night patrols and you join them, helping record nests and protect eggs. Season-dependent.

seo.metaTitle: Akwidaa Turtle Watch | Ghana
seo.metaDescription: Night patrol on the beach. 2 days small-group tour in Akwidaa, Ghana.

title: Hell's Gate on Two Wheels
summary: Hell's Gate is one of the few Kenyan parks where you can cycle among wildlife. You ride past zebra, buffalo and warthogs, drop into Njorowa Gorge on foot between narrow red cliffs, and stop at Fischer's Tower. A guide rides with you; the lunch picnic is near the geothermal vents.

seo.metaTitle: Hell's Gate on Two Wheels | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Pedal past zebra, no cages. 7 hours small-group tour in Naivasha, Kenya.

title: Crescent Island: Walking with Giraffe
summary: Crescent Island is a private sanctuary on Lake Naivasha where you walk among giraffe, zebra, wildebeest and impala. A boat crosses the lake first, passing hippos. No predators live here, so the walking is relaxed.

seo.metaTitle: Crescent Island: Walking with Giraffe | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: No fences between you and the herd. 4 hours small-group tour in Naivasha, Kenya.

title: Longonot Crater Rim Walk
summary: Mount Longonot is a young volcano with a steep climb and a full rim circuit. The inside crater is green, steam still rises in places and the Rift Valley opens out below. Bring water and decent shoes.

seo.metaTitle: Longonot Crater Rim Walk | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Volcano under your boots. 6 hours small-group tour in Naivasha, Kenya.

title: Elsamere and the Colobus Trees
summary: Elsamere was the home of Joy Adamson, the author of Born Free. Black-and-white colobus monkeys bounce through the trees in the garden, and the museum inside tells the story of the lioness Elsa. Afternoon tea is included on the lawn.

seo.metaTitle: Elsamere and the Colobus Trees | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Joy Adamson**'**s lakeside house. 4 hours small-group tour in Naivasha, Kenya.

title: Lake Nakuru: Pink Fringe, Rhino Edge
summary: Lake Nakuru National Park is a rhino sanctuary with both black and white rhinos, plus buffalo, leopards and flamingos when the water levels suit. Drives climb to Baboon Cliff for the long view.

seo.metaTitle: Lake Nakuru: Pink Fringe, Rhino Edge | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Rhino country on a soda lake. 8 hours small-group tour in Nakuru, Kenya.

title: Menengai Crater at Sunrise
summary: Menengai Crater is one of the largest volcanic calderas in the world, ringed by forest. We hike the rim at dawn, spot birds and look down on Nakuru town from the top.

seo.metaTitle: Menengai Crater at Sunrise | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: A volcano that Nakuru sits beside. 4 hours small-group tour in Nakuru, Kenya.

title: Lake Bogoria: Geysers and Kudu
summary: Lake Bogoria's western shore is lined with hot springs and spouting geysers that scald if you step wrong. A ranger walks you past the steam to the water's edge, where flamingos feed, then up the hillside to look for greater kudu with their spiralled horns.

seo.metaTitle: Lake Bogoria: Geysers and Kudu | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Boiling springs next to a quiet lake. 2 days small-group tour in Bogoria, Kenya.

title: Baringo by Boat: Hippos and Fish Eagles
summary: Lake Baringo is a freshwater lake with hippos, crocodiles and over 400 bird species. A local fisherman takes you out in a boat at dawn and calls the fish eagles down for food.

seo.metaTitle: Baringo by Boat: Hippos and Fish Eagles | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Thinner crowds, more birds. 2 days small-group tour in Baringo, Kenya.

title: Lake Turkana: The Jade Sea
summary: Lake Turkana is a huge desert lake that looks jade-coloured in the right light. Over five days you reach Loiyangalani, meet the El Molo and Turkana communities and visit Sibiloi National Park, where early human fossils were found.

seo.metaTitle: Lake Turkana: The Jade Sea | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Long drive, longer horizon. 5 days small-group tour in Loiyangalani, Kenya.

title: Koobi Fora: Where Old Bones Came Out of the Ground
summary: Koobi Fora is one of the world's richest sites for early human fossils. A guide takes you through the dry landscape and explains how researchers pieced together our family tree.

seo.metaTitle: Koobi Fora: Where Old Bones Came Out of the Ground | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Fossil country. 3 days small-group tour in Sibiloi, Kenya.

title: Samburu Special Five
summary: Samburu National Reserve holds five species you won't see in the Mara: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Somali ostrich, beisa oryx and gerenuk. You drive along the Ewaso Ng'iro River and visit a Samburu village.

seo.metaTitle: Samburu Special Five | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Grevy**'**s zebra, gerenuk, oryx and friends. 3 days small-group tour in Samburu, Kenya.

title: Ol Pejeta: The Last Two Northern Whites
summary: Ol Pejeta Conservancy is home to the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, both female. You meet them with rangers, visit the chimpanzee sanctuary and take a night drive.

seo.metaTitle: Ol Pejeta: The Last Two Northern Whites | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Rhino orbit. 2 days small-group tour in Laikipia, Kenya.

title: Camels Across Laikipia
summary: Laikipia has camel-supported walking safaris that cover ground on foot with the animals carrying gear. You camp in the bush, track elephants on foot and learn bush skills from Samburu guides.

seo.metaTitle: Camels Across Laikipia | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Slow walking, bigger sky. 3 days small-group tour in Laikipia, Kenya.

title: Lewa Conservancy: Rhino Ranch
summary: Lewa began as a cattle ranch and became one of Kenya's most successful rhino sanctuaries. You drive with a ranger, hear how anti-poaching patrols work, and visit a community school the conservancy supports. Walking drives are possible on request.

seo.metaTitle: Lewa Conservancy: Rhino Ranch | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: A conservancy that rebuilt itself. 2 days small-group tour in Lewa, Kenya.

title: Mount Kenya's Sirimon Trail
summary: The Sirimon route climbs from forest to moorland full of giant lobelias, with Point Lenana as the goal at nearly 5,000 metres. You walk with a guide and porters, sleep in huts and start the final climb in darkness to reach the summit at sunrise.

seo.metaTitle: Mount Kenya's Sirimon Trail | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Three days to Point Lenana. 4 days small-group tour in Mount Kenya, Kenya.

title: Aberdare Waterfalls and Mist
summary: The Aberdares are cold, wet and covered in moorland that looks more like Scotland than Kenya. You hike to Karuru Falls, one of the highest in the country, and stop at Gura Falls for another viewpoint, with a picnic lunch in the highland mist.

seo.metaTitle: Aberdare Waterfalls and Mist | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Cold air, big drops. 8 hours small-group tour in Aberdares, Kenya.

title: Kericho's Tea Ridge
summary: Kericho's tea estates roll across hills in perfect green rows. A picker shows how to pluck two leaves and a bud, a factory guide follows the leaf through withering and drying, and you finish with a tasting in an estate cottage.

seo.metaTitle: Kericho's Tea Ridge | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Green carpets in every direction. 6 hours small-group tour in Kericho, Kenya.

title: Iten: Running on the Roof of the Rift
summary: Iten, in the Kenyan highlands, is home to many Olympic runners. You join a morning run with local athletes, visit a training camp and look out over the Kerio Valley.

seo.metaTitle: Iten: Running on the Roof of the Rift | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Train where champions train. 2 days small-group tour in Iten, Kenya.

title: Kerio Valley Viewpoint Road
summary: The road down into the Kerio Valley drops from the highlands in tight hairpins, with the valley floor opening far below. We stop at a viewpoint, buy roasted maize and tea at a roadside kiosk and talk with locals about life on the escarpment.

seo.metaTitle: Kerio Valley Viewpoint Road | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: The cliffs that drop away. 8 hours small-group tour in Elgeyo Marakwet, Kenya.

title: Mount Elgon and the Elephant Caves
summary: Mount Elgon's Kitum Cave is a deep cave where elephants come at night to dig salt from the walls with their tusks. A ranger leads you inside and explains how the herds navigate in the dark. Waterproof boots help.

seo.metaTitle: Mount Elgon and the Elephant Caves | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Elephants that dig salt in caves. 3 days small-group tour in Mount Elgon, Kenya.

title: Saiwa Swamp: Meet the Sitatunga
summary: Saiwa Swamp is a tiny park built around a marsh that shelters sitatunga, a shy swamp antelope. You walk raised boardwalks, climb treetop platforms and wait. Patience pays off, and there are monkeys and birds as a fallback.

seo.metaTitle: Saiwa Swamp: Meet the Sitatunga | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: An antelope that lives in water. 2 days small-group tour in Saiwa Swamp, Kenya.

title: Kakamega Rainforest at Dawn
summary: Kakamega Forest is the last piece of equatorial rainforest in Kenya, full of birds, monkeys and butterflies. You walk with a local guide at dawn and visit the Isiukhu Falls.

seo.metaTitle: Kakamega Rainforest at Dawn | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Kenya**'**s last bit of equatorial forest. 2 days small-group tour in Kakamega, Kenya.

title: Kisumu Lakeside and the Impala Sanctuary
summary: Kisumu is Kenya's lake port, where fishermen still land Nile perch by hand. You visit Hippo Point at sunset, the Impala Sanctuary and the Dunga fishing beach, and eat fried tilapia with ugali right on the shore.

seo.metaTitle: Kisumu Lakeside and the Impala Sanctuary | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Hippos at dusk. 6 hours small-group tour in Kisumu, Kenya.

title: Kit Mikayi: The Rock with a Story
summary: Kit Mikayi is a stack of massive boulders near Kisumu and a sacred place for the Luo. A local guide leads you up and tells the legend of the man who lived there.

seo.metaTitle: Kit Mikayi: The Rock with a Story | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Boulders that balance. 4 hours small-group tour in Seme, Kenya.

title: Thimlich Ohinga: Stone Walls Without Mortar
summary: Thimlich Ohinga is a UNESCO site of dry-stone enclosures built without mortar, possibly 500 years ago. A local guide walks the walls, explains the inner rooms and cattle pens and shares what archaeologists know and don't know about the builders.

seo.metaTitle: Thimlich Ohinga: Stone Walls Without Mortar | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: A fortress built by hand. 2 days small-group tour in Migori, Kenya.

title: Rusinga Island: Fossils and a Mausoleum
summary: Rusinga Island is joined to the mainland by a causeway and holds fossil sites where early ape remains were found. You visit the Tom Mboya mausoleum, a fishing beach and a local lodge, and learn how the island's history stretches from apes to politics.

seo.metaTitle: Rusinga Island: Fossils and a Mausoleum | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Victoria**'**s quiet island. 2 days small-group tour in Rusinga Island, Kenya.

title: Mfangano Island Rock Art
summary: Mfangano Island holds ancient rock paintings of geometric shapes, probably made by hunter-gatherers. A local guide leads a hike to the sites and a boat circuit around the island's fishing villages, with lunch at a village kitchen.

seo.metaTitle: Mfangano Island Rock Art | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Paintings above the water. 2 days small-group tour in Mfangano, Kenya.

title: Mombasa Old Town: Doors, Dhows and Dust
summary: Mombasa's Old Town has narrow lanes, carved wooden doors and a Portuguese-built fort. You tour Fort Jesus, walk the old harbour where dhows still unload and sip kahawa from brass pots at a street stall.

seo.metaTitle: Mombasa Old Town: Doors, Dhows and Dust | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Swahili streets with Portuguese ghosts. 5 hours small-group tour in Mombasa, Kenya.

title: Likoni Ferry and the Southern Shore
summary: The Likoni Ferry carries tens of thousands of commuters between Mombasa Island and the south coast every day. You cross with a local guide, wander the Likoni waterfront and ride a tuk-tuk to the first beach stop.

seo.metaTitle: Likoni Ferry and the Southern Shore | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Ride the ferry like a local. 3 hours small-group tour in Mombasa, Kenya.

title: Haller Park: A Quarry Turned Forest
summary: Haller Park was a limestone quarry before it was replanted. Today giraffe, hippo, crocodile and giant tortoises walk and wallow in the restored forest, and a guide explains the rehabilitation project.

seo.metaTitle: Haller Park: A Quarry Turned Forest | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Giraffe, hippo and a 130-year-old tortoise. 4 hours small-group tour in Mombasa, Kenya.

title: Mombasa Tusks and Moi Avenue
summary: The Mombasa Tusks are giant aluminium arches on Moi Avenue, built to mark a royal visit in 1952. A guide takes you through the city centre, explains its growth and finishes with a snack at a local café.

seo.metaTitle: Mombasa Tusks and Moi Avenue | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Silver tusks on a busy street. 3 hours small-group tour in Mombasa, Kenya.

title: Lamu: Donkeys, Dhows and No Cars
summary: Lamu Old Town is a UNESCO site with no cars, only donkeys and walkers. You tour the fort, the museum and the narrow alleys, and sail a dhow at sunset.

seo.metaTitle: Lamu: Donkeys, Dhows and No Cars | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: An island that still runs on foot. 3 days small-group tour in Lamu, Kenya.

title: Shela Beach and Sunset Dhow
summary: Shela is a quiet village near Lamu Old Town with a long beach and tall dunes. You walk the sand, have a seafood lunch at a beach house and sail a dhow back at sunset as the call to prayer drifts across the water.

seo.metaTitle: Shela Beach and Sunset Dhow | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Slow beach day. 8 hours small-group tour in Lamu, Kenya.

title: Takwa Ruins on Manda Island
summary: Takwa is a ruined Swahili town on Manda Island, abandoned in the 17th century after the water supply failed. You cross by boat, walk through the Friday mosque, houses and a pillar tomb, with a guide explaining the town's story.

seo.metaTitle: Takwa Ruins on Manda Island | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: An abandoned Swahili town. 6 hours small-group tour in Manda Island, Kenya.

title: Gedi Ruins and the Forest That Hides Them
summary: The Gedi ruins are the remains of a Swahili town in the forest near Watamu. A guide walks you through the mosque, palace and houses, and points out monkeys and birds.

seo.metaTitle: Gedi Ruins and the Forest That Hides Them | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: A lost town under the trees. 5 hours small-group tour in Watamu, Kenya.

title: Arabuko-Sokoke: Elephant Shrew Country
summary: Arabuko-Sokoke is the largest surviving block of coastal forest in East Africa and home to species found nowhere else. A local birder leads you quietly down the trails to look for the golden-rumped elephant shrew and the Sokoke scops owl.

seo.metaTitle: Arabuko-Sokoke: Elephant Shrew Country | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Small forest, big endemics. 6 hours small-group tour in Arabuko-Sokoke, Kenya.

title: Mida Creek Boardwalk and Mangrove Paddle
summary: At Mida Creek a boardwalk crosses mangroves and mudflats where waders feed at low tide. You walk the boards, paddle a canoe among the roots and eat fresh crab at a village restaurant.

seo.metaTitle: Mida Creek Boardwalk and Mangrove Paddle | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Birds at low tide. 4 hours small-group tour in Watamu, Kenya.

title: Watamu Marine Park Snorkel
summary: Watamu Marine Park has reefs full of coloured fish, rays and sea turtles. A boatman takes you out in a glass-bottom boat, and a guide helps you snorkel in a protected spot.

seo.metaTitle: Watamu Marine Park Snorkel | Kenya
seo.metaDescription: Reefs close to the beach. 4 hours small-group tour in Watamu, Kenya.

title: Marafa: Hell's Kitchen
summary: Marafa Depression, called Hell's Kitchen, is a gorge of sandstone pillars in red, white and ochre. We arrive late so the colours glow at sunset, and a local guide tells the legend of the village that disappeared into the earth.
